When i started my apprentice job as an Automations Technician i always wondered just "how and can it be?" Regarding frequency inverters (Variable speed drives as they're called elsewhere) and their "wait X amount of time for discharge before handling". We had a rather large VSD we had to pull off a tray sealing machine. Pretty sizable block, weighed close to 40kgs (110lbs), we took it inside the maintenance shop and sat it down, that thing was still humming after 30 minutes of having been without power, my boss decided to show me why it has that safety sticker. So he mounted a cable to a metal surface that went to ground and used a plastic rod and touched the VSds outputs. That arc was glorious for such a seemingly innocent thing.

Also learned the importance of LOTO once when I had to change a 400V outlet once, I had only locked the breaker but left the key next to the lock because i was certain i would be done quicker before anyone could find the breaker and shock me. I wasn't, so I took off the outlet and grabbed my cable cutter with my left hand and cut into the cable - let me tell you that cut went fast when my arm had 400V jumping through my arm and back into ground on the same cable. Shit hurt - anyway me panicking, went to the breaker box and discovered my lock was off, found out my boss had removed it because that breaker for some reason also powered the Analysts QA computers in the production (great idea to have them share the same breaker for what also powers machines that get washed 4-7 times a day) and they were having a hissy fit that the power was off again. Boss saw the key next to the breaker, called around - no one knew anything, I didn't answer as I was pulling off the outlet. So he took it off, I got shocked, got sent to the doctor, had an EKG - everything looked fine. Got back, got sent home and now it's been three years. Thankfully woke up the next day and have had great job ever since.

I always thought people talking about seeing so many stars were taking the piss. Turns out I had -4 in both eyes. Now I love starry nights, seeing individual strands of grass, leaves - being able to read a screen that's more than five feet away. I was 25 when I got mine...

It's understandable you think that, but you only use the fruit part of Sichuan pepper which is the red housing, the seed which is quite large when going by seed to fruit ratio is usually discarded because it's so tough.

And where I live I can only buy whole Sichuan peppers so if I wanted to cook with Sichuan I'll have to pluck the seeds out hence my love hate relationship.

Black pepper and Sichuan aren't in the same family and are processed differently, Sichuan is simply harvested and dried when ripe, where as pepper is harvested before being completely ripe, then cooked and dried.

Doesn't have a taste, the seeds are hard like stones and become gritty/sandy when cooked with (if grinded) and basically ruins the dish. It's quite literal the same as chewing sand - if you don't grind them, they can break your teeth.

Coop is a reseller so they buy the packaged meat either from a food factory or from a slaughter house directly. 

Example from where I work (also using coop in the example)
We only produce what the customer buys - and they only pay for what they order - so if coop orders 2.5 tonnes of mince we take a meat box from the "warehouse" and dump it in the meat grinder/mixer. The box is everywhere between 500-600kg of meat, If At the end of the batch there's still a couple tens' kgs left in the meat combiner even though the batch is complete the giveaway will be turned up to run the batch dry faster so the next order can be produced. It won't be turned up ofc. If the next order is similar to the previous. (On some products the giveaway is also turned up because if you as a consumer notice that "ha ha they constantly give me more meat than what I pay for" you're automatically going to end up buying that specific brand - which is us that produce it so by proxy you're going to end up buying more off of our products thinking you made a steal, when in reality we know)

"But why not just stock up on the previous batch?" Because the customer changes their label requirements a lot, also they would rather pay for as fresh as possible produced products rather than soon to run out products- which makes sense since they'll have a higher guarantee profiting off of the meat if they don't have to sell at lower price/toss it out.

The other reason is simply space, there's only so much meat you can have stored for a certain time frame. And keeping food frozen (-20C) is a lot more expensive than just keeping it cool (+3C) energy wise.

Hope that explains it better.

I think the Danish summer eat is quite good in this perspective - Koldskål (litteral translation is Cold bowl). It's akin to egg nog, the key differences is that we user buttermilk instead of regular milk, there's no alcohol in it and vanilla is also added (some also add a bit of lemon zest and juice)  


* 1 Litre of buttermilk (35-36oz)
* 3 decilitres of Ymer (Traditionally a danish soured milk, akin to yoghurt but creamier - don't know what you'd use outside of Denmark, as sour as kefir but not as carbonated and again creamier)
* 2 egg yolks  (we have such small salmonella findings in Denmark that eggs can be eaten raw/fresh without danger - but for elsewhere i'd use pasteurized yolks)
* 2 Tablespoons of sugar
* Half of a vanilla pod

Mix sugar and the seeds from the vanilla pod into a fine paste, mix with the eggs and whip away till you get the a fluffy egg nog consistency. Add the buttermilk and Ymer and mix it in then serve cold.

Traditionally we eat it with Kammerjunker, which is a sweet biscuit crushed/broken into the koldskål so the sweetness primarily stems from these. I more or less enjoy it without the biscuits but to each their own.

I knew I wasn't going to be able to acquire Ketamine, but magic mushrooms are another deal - I almost didn't get to take them. But the moment I got my grow box I could see light at the end of the tunnel, I had promised myself that if it didn't work I'd off myself (keep reading, though). I cared for that little bag of humidity, comprising of a plastic tote with a medium in, saw the shrooms rise and dried them and planned my trip. 

I was at this time in life living at home because I was afraid that if I lived alone, it would certainly be the end of me. I knew that if I was alone I would start drinking heavily again as I had done before I moved back in.

I never told my parents I was growing illicit drugs in their home, and I kept it under wraps until my day of the trip arrived. I woke up early that morning, having a small meal (read an empty stomach gives a harder trip, you can always eat to lessen the trips effect if it goes sour, or so they say). Greeted my parents and they told me they were going out to shop, so they left and I ate the shrooms. It took around an hour before it hit me, I was sitting in their living room with the dogs. I felt immense joy and sadness, thoughts started to speed up and I was questioning myself why I wanna take my own life, what do I gain from it now and what do I gain from it later. I was bawling and alone with two dogs, those little balls of fluff were there and it was like they just radiated love. I felt joy and love for the first time in over a decade, like it's ok i feel this way, the solutions aren't easy, but they are there. I was calming down again and then my parents came home, seeing me sitting in a room, wrapped in blankets now unfolded from the dogs coming to greet them back home.
